def maxAverageOfPath(matrix):
    n = len(matrix)
    
    # dp[i][j] will store the maximum total cost from (0, 0) to (i, j)
    dp = [[float('-inf')] * n for _ in range(n)]
    dp[0][0] = matrix[0][0]
    
    # Fill first row: can only come from left
    for j in range(1, n):
        dp[0][j] = dp[0][j-1] + matrix[0][j]
        
    # Fill first column: can only come from above
    for i in range(1, n):
        dp[i][0] = dp[i-1][0] + matrix[i][0]
    
    # Fill rest of the table
    for i in range(1, n):
        for j in range(1, n):
            dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]) + matrix[i][j]
            
    # The maximum total cost to reach bottom-right is at dp[n-1][n-1]
    max_total_cost = dp[n-1][n-1]
    
    # Number of cells in any path from top-left to bottom-right in an N*N grid:
    # We start at (0,0) and end at (N-1,N-1). 
    # Each step is either right or down. Total steps = 2*(N-1), so total cells visited = 2*(N-1)+1 = 2N - 1
    num_cells = 2 * n - 1
    
    return max_total_cost / num_cells
